blocking.title: The Ed25519 refusal in VerificationKeyRing::begin_rotation is a refusal branch no committed test exercises: mutant M28 survives the 53-test suite, and the probe shows a P-256 key entering the ring under it
blocking.detail: keys.rs:79 `if !is_ed25519(&new_key.public_key) || …` is the branch; the only test named for it, non_ed25519_keys_are_refused_at_every_entry_point (tests/authz.rs:2699-2743), builds `p256_key` with `valid_from: now - Duration::from_secs(1)` (2717) and hands it to begin_rotation (2729-2733) — `new_key.valid_from < now` (keys.rs:87) refuses that key before the algorithm is looked at. Replay: with the `!is_ed25519(&new_key.public_key) ||` term deleted, `cargo test --test authz` -> `53 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. Non-equivalence proved by a probe (never committed): P-256 key, valid_from = now + 1 s, key_id 6, old key valid until now + 2000 s -> under the mutant begin_rotation returns Ok and `ring.public_keys()` reports `["Ed25519", "P-256"]` (assertion output: `ring now reports ["Ed25519", "P-256"]`); on head the same probe passes with auth.key_unavailable. The narration credits this test for the branch: commit 09aae8b `Red first (a Secp256r1 KeyPair was accepted at all three entry points), then refused with auth.key_unavailable`; SECURITY.md:12-14 `VerificationKeyRing::new and begin_rotation refuse any non-Ed25519 key`; evidence record §MINOR (security) `Now refused … at all three entry points … Test: non_ed25519_keys_are_refused_at_every_entry_point`; governance note :148-149. For the begin_rotation entry point the committed test cannot have been red before the fix. The record's 26-mutant scope is src/authorize.rs only, so its table is not contradicted; the claim is. This is the defect class the round-1 blocking named (a test credited for a branch it does not reach), on a refusal branch introduced by this PR — blocking by the round-2 rule. Fix is one line: give the rotation probe a key whose every other precondition holds (valid_from = now + 1 s, as in two_key_rotation_has_a_bounded_overlap), so that M28 turns the test red; re-issue the record's Ed25519 paragraph with that mutant.

major.title: The orphan-rev gate is green on the inputs it cannot parse: `rev = "main"` and a `{ rev, git }` key order both print `0 intra-organisation git patch(es)` / `Orphan-rev gate: OK` and exit 0 — contradicting ADR-0031 D2 (`jamais une branche`) and D3 (`un gate muet n'est pas un gate`), which names this script as the reference realisation
major.detail: check-patch-rev.ts:38-40: a single regex requires `git = "https://github.com/<o>/<r>"` before `rev = "<40 hex>"` inside one `{…}`; anything else is `continue`d (43). Measured on the #13 worktree, Cargo.toml edited then restored: rev = "main" -> `Orphan-rev gate: 0 intra-organisation git patch(es) in [patch.crates-io]` / `Orphan-rev gate: OK`, exit 0; `biscuit-auth = { rev = "81ce…", git = "https://github.com/libre-ai/authz-biscuit" }` -> same output, exit 0. A `branch = "main"` or `tag = …` git-dep, or the `[patch.crates-io.biscuit-auth]` table form, take the same silent path. The unit test check-patch-rev.test.ts:19-22 (`a short or branch rev is not a pin and is not accepted as one`) asserts `parseGitPatches(...) === []`, i.e. it locks the silent drop in as the specification. cargo deny (`unknown-git = deny` + allow-org libre-ai) accepts any libre-ai git source, branch included, so nothing else catches it. Fleet memory: silent-guardrail class (a gate must prove it ran on what it was meant to see). Fix: count every git source under [patch.crates-io] (parse the section as TOML — `Bun.TOML.parse` / `import … with { type: "toml" }` — or match `git =` independently of `rev =`), and fail with a named reason on any intra-organisation git source whose rev is not a full SHA; add the red tests (branch rev, key order, table form, `branch =`).

major.title: ADR-0031 declares `Aucun invariant nouveau` while D1 and D3 impose fleet-wide obligations (one home per patched crate; a blocking orphan-rev gate at every secondary consumer) that no invariant carries, and I-05 as written covers vendored *contracts*, not patched crates; no machine gate checks the claim
major.detail: INVARIANTS.md:11 I-05: `les copies vendorées de contrats sous gate de dérive sont des projections vérifiées (jamais éditées à la main, jamais canoniques)` — contracts. ADR-0031 §Invariants extends it by analogy (`comme check:schemas l'est pour les contrats`) and adds nothing for D1 (`un seul foyer dans la flotte`) or D3 (`Chaque consommateur secondaire porte un gate bloquant`). AGENTS.md: `INVARIANTS.md is exhaustive by construction: doctrine absent from it does not exist, whatever another document asserts`. Gate replay: `bun run check` on #91 -> exit 0, 913 pass; grep of tools/quality/*.ts for `## Invariants` / `Aucun invariant` -> no tool reads an ADR's Invariants section, so the exhaustiveness rule has no executant for ADRs (the brief's `I-25` is the skills invariant, INVARIANTS.md:31 — not this gate). Precedent cuts both ways: ADR-0020 §2.5's own bounds (allow-org, pin-SHA + review) are also absent from INVARIANTS.md (grep allow-org/git-dep/patch.crates-io -> none), and ADR-0030 uses the same `Aucun invariant nouveau` form with two named existing invariants. Owner decision, two options: (a) carry D1+D3 into INVARIANTS.md (new I-xx dated 2026-09-08, or widen I-05 from `contrats` to `contrats et crates patchés`) and cite it from the ADR; (b) state in §Invariants that D1–D4 are ADR-level security bounds of the same nature as §2.5 and deliberately not invariants — making the exhaustiveness rule's exception explicit instead of silent. Form otherwise matches ADR-0030 (same header fields, same four sections); DECISION-REGISTER.md needs no entry by its own header (`never been an index of every accepted ADR`).

minor.title: The `.get` / `.all` / `.any` sentence of SECURITY.md attributes to step 5 denials that come from evaluation
minor.detail: SECURITY.md:176-181: `they pass through step 5 like every signed block. A block written in datalog 3.3 idioms is therefore denied as a class … .all/.any, .try_or, .get …`. Probe on block 2: `[{1}, true, Binary::Any]` (no closure) -> auth.operation_denied; `[{1}, 0, Binary::Get]` -> auth.operation_denied. op_ok passes Binary::Any/All/Get (authorize.rs:452 `Op::Unary(_) | Op::Binary(_) => true`); the denial is the evaluator's, fail-closed but not step 5. The paragraph's conclusion (denied as a class) holds; its `therefore` does not. Same precision point for `plus multi-byte UTF-8` (SECURITY.md:109): the property samples one code point, `é` (tests/authz.rs:1918-1920).

minor.title: The double-load figure measures the token-only load, not the guard pass, and is a single run
minor.detail: double_load_cost_is_measured (tests/authz.rs:2748-2775) times `verified.authorizer()` only. The guard pass added by this PR is load + `dump()` walk + `snapshot()` (authorize.rs:486-492 -> snapshot.rs:187-260: every block re-translated into a fresh symbol table, facts/keys/policies serialised to proto), none of which is in the number. The record's sentence `the double load is measured instead of asserted` is true of the load, not of the guard's cost.
